title: Keyset pagination request and page result

page_size.x-unbounded-note: No maximum page size appears anywhere in the Sprint 0A baseline. An upper bound is a real enumeration-risk control and SHOULD exist, but choosing the number is the contract owner's decision, not this package's. Recorded as open.

cursor.x-opacity-rule: API-003 requires the cursor to be "opaque/tamper-safe". This contract enforces only that it is a string: NO character set is mandated, because the manifest simultaneously declares the encoding and signing algorithm unspecified, and a charset rule would forbid standard base64 and dot-separated signed tokens. TAMPER-SAFETY IS THEREFORE NOT ENFORCED BY THIS CONTRACT. An integrity mechanism (MAC or signature) MUST be specified before freeze; independent security review demonstrated that base64 of "offset=40&limit=20" satisfies opacity by inspection while remaining a forgeable offset.

sort.x-tiebreaker-rule: At least two sort keys are required so page boundaries are deterministic. Derived from asset-library-database-ux-spec-th.md section 5.2, which specifies the keyset cursor (created_at, id) and prohibits deep offset, and from Contracts/Events/Jobs Workstream API-003 "Stable ordering; no duplicate/missing between pages". This is a DECLARED inference from those two sources, not a rule stated verbatim in the Decision Register.

then.x-cursor-continuity-rule: API-003 requires no duplicate or missing item between pages. A page claiming has_more without the cursor that reaches the next page loses every following item, so the two fields are constrained together rather than independently.
